note: Offshore 190 applicant, 90+5 points, lodged Sep 2023; still in Received status roughly 20 months later with no case officer assigned and no commencement email.

comments.body: Processing is not strictly date-ordered; the department is mostly working through earlier 2023 lodgements, so feeling skipped is common. Little to do but wait.

replies.body: Asked whether status can be requested or expedited once past the published 21-month timeframe.

comments.body: Healthcare and teaching get priority within 190, others are equal; a recent grant seen was lodged October 2023.

note: Earlier 190 applicant reported around 17 months to receive an S56 request, then about one month more to grant, with no other contact in between.

title: Claiming partner skill points for 189
note: Applicant asks whether partner points can be claimed at EOI stage before obtaining a partner skills assessment, and which assessing authority suits a partner with finance/MBA background.

comments.body: All four partner-point conditions including a positive skills assessment and competent English must be met before claiming the points, not just at invitation.

replies.body: Confirmed the partner needs a positive assessment for their occupation; a degree alone is not enough.

note: SA-nominated 491 applicant; invited and lodged late 2022, medical early 2023, received an S56 PCC renewal request, responded, and was granted after roughly 19 months.
SA-nominated 491 applicant lodged mid-2022, contacted by a case officer in late 2023, and granted in January 2024, roughly 19 months after lodging.
Onshore 491 applicant, 85 points, lodged mid-2023, received a commencement email in January 2024, and was granted in February 2024 in under a year.
NSW-nominated 491 family applicant lodged late 2022, medical early 2023, then multiple S56 renewal requests for police checks and medicals, granted after about 22 months.
Offshore NSW-nominated 491 applicant, 95 points, lodged with medical April 2023 and police check May 2023; still in Received status a year later.
SA-nominated 491 applicant lodged late 2022; submitted an S56 response and a second medical in 2024, still under further assessment awaiting grant.
Offshore NSW-nominated 491 applicant, 70 points, lodged mid-2023; received an S56 police-check request about a year later and is still awaiting grant.
ACT-nominated 491 applicant invited and lodged late 2022 with medical completed; still showing Received status with no further movement.
Applicant lodged a complete application in March 2019 and received a direct grant in December 2019, roughly nine months later.

comments.body: Congratulated the applicant and expressed hope of a grant soon.

note: Lodged early February 2019, had a case officer contact to add a newborn and provide more work evidence, uploaded requested documents in July 2019, then continued waiting.

Self-lodged onshore partner application in March 2023, received an early request for a police check within about a month, then waiting and surprised at the fast review against the long published timeline.

comments.body: A responder suggested a thorough, easy-to-decide application gets triaged faster and noted their own case cleared in under three months.
Applicant replied that the triage explanation made sense and offered to share their self-lodging experience.

note: Onshore partner application submitted June 2023, received a request for more information in August, submitted all evidence within the deadline, and was granted in September 2023.

Combined onshore partner application lodged mid-May 2023, request for ID, a discharge document and a health exam in August, with the first-stage visa granted in September 2023; a later attempt to have the permanent stage processed was declined.

comments.body: Another member suggested the relationship may not have reached the required duration at lodgement, which could explain why the permanent stage was not granted together.

title: Does sponsoring a spouse who gained PR as a secondary applicant count as prior sponsorship?
note: Applicant lodged an offshore partner application for their spouse and worries whether a former partner who gained residence as a secondary applicant on their skilled visa counts as a previous sponsorship on the sponsor form.
Lodged in mid-July 2017 with medicals uploaded about ten days later, still with no case officer contact and continuing to wait.
Lodged at the end of May 2017 with a processing-commenced email in mid-July; after more than three months the application status was still received with no documents requested.
Lodged early April 2017 with employment verification confirmed in early September; past the standard processing time and still awaiting a grant with no useful response to status enquiries.

Engineering applicant with 65 points submitted an expression of interest in early September 2017, received an invitation on 20 September, lodged on 27 September with all documents front-loaded, and is waiting on a grant estimate.

comments.body: A moderator pointed the applicant to the tracker's grant-date estimator tool.

title: How long does offshore 186 direct-entry nomination take for critical-list occupations?
note: Offshore applicant asks how long the employer-sponsored permanent nomination is taking for occupations on the priority shortage list.

comments.body: Responders said accredited-sponsor and healthcare cases move fastest, possibly four to six weeks if paperwork is complete, while others can face long delays.

title: 186 DE nomination and visa processing time for offshore academic
note: Offshore academic whose university lodged a 186 DE nomination in May 2020 asks how long nomination plus visa take and whether a dependent needs an English test.

comments.body: Nomination approval often takes one to two months but can stretch longer; offshore timelines are harder to predict.

replies.body: A dependent with an English-medium degree can usually prove functional English with study certificates instead of sitting a test.

note: Onshore engineer with an accredited sponsor lodged nomination and visa together; case officer assigned within weeks, nomination approved, documents and medical completed, awaiting decision.
Offshore university lecturer had nomination lodged and approved within a week, then lodged the visa and completed health checks, but the application has stayed at received with no further update.
Offshore applicant lodged the nomination in late July and the visa about a month later, with no update on either by mid-September.
Offshore software engineer on a medium-term 482 lodged in early December, completed health clearance days later, and received the grant about six weeks after lodgement.

comments.body: Larger sponsoring companies tend to see faster processing; asking HR to email the department that work is suffering may help.

note: Medium-term 482 applicant had sponsorship lodged and approved in November, lodged the visa in December, then received a case officer request for a spouse form which was answered, and is awaiting a decision.
Medium-term 482 applicant lodged the visa in early December and completed medicals in mid-January, but more than two months later the status still showed received.

title: 485 subsequent entrant processing time and how to lodge
note: A 485 holder asks how to lodge a subsequent-entrant application for family overseas, whether it can be submitted from within Australia, and the usual processing time.

comments.body: Subsequent-entrant 485 applications must be lodged on paper using the relevant form; family can apply from inside or outside Australia.

replies.body: Reported processing for subsequent entrants tends to run roughly three to twelve weeks.

note: Graduate cook lodged a 485 online in February, completed a health exam in March due to a past medical condition, and received the grant about two months after lodging.
Applicant got state nomination approved within a day on priority, lodged 190 in early Sep 2022, uploaded most docs and booked medicals; still in received status awaiting grant.

comments.body: Did you request priority processing for the nomination, and did you lodge the visa without police checks ready?

replies.body: Requested priority citing an expiring skills assessment; nomination approved in under 24 hours. Lodged the visa and noted in a text box that police checks from multiple countries were still being processed.

note: NSW 190 applicant with 105 points received a straight grant about 20 days after lodging, with no case officer contact in between.
Onshore applicant lodged a Victoria 190 in 2019; after roughly three years the file was opened and a case officer requested fresh medicals, police checks and a partner police check.
Applicant lodged a 190 in November 2019 and received a first case officer contact in August 2022, still waiting for a decision.
Offshore applicant lodged a 491 with South Australia nomination and completed health clearance; worried that published processing times jumped sharply and asking whether to also submit a 189 EOI.

comments.body: Nothing stops you submitting another EOI, but you may need to withdraw the 491 if a 189 invite comes; consult a registered agent.

note: Family-sponsored 491 in SA: invited early October 2022, lodged end of November, case officer contact mid December, health cleared two days later, grant in February 2023.
State-nominated 491 in SA: invited May 2022, lodged June, medical July; grant came through in February 2023, roughly eight months after lodging.
Family-sponsored 491 in SA: invited October 2022, lodged November with medicals done the same month; still pending a decision.
State-nominated 491 in SA: invited October 2022, lodged December, medical January 2023; status moved to further assessment.
State-nominated 491 in SA: invited 10 October 2022, lodged 15 November, medical 12 December; status still received as of May 2023.
491 applicant received an information request in June 2023 for a single accredited document translation and an updated police check, asking whether further requests are likely.

comments.body: Multiple information requests can happen; you can never assume everything is accepted until the grant arrives.

note: 189 applicant invited 1 March 2017, lodged 14 March, finished uploading all documents by 1 April; received an assessment-commenced email on 22 May and is still waiting.
189 applicant lodged 17 December 2016; case officer requested police checks and medicals in January 2017 and the applicant uploaded an overseas police check in April, then heard nothing further.

title: Telling DHA about a pregnancy while a 190 is pending
note: Applicant lodged a 190 NSW with spouse and child and finished medicals; asks when to notify the department about a planned pregnancy and whether it delays the grant or means redoing medicals.

comments.body: You must report a change in circumstances such as pregnancy; the file is then put on hold so the newborn can be added, and hiding it can cause problems later.

replies.body: It is usually better to have the baby before the grant, since getting a visa for a child born offshore after the grant is a long process.

note: Family granted a 491 regional visa nominated by NSW while offshore; now planning the move and job search in IT.

comments.body: Offshore IT roles are very hard to land; local experience and networking matter more than a local SIM or address.

replies.body: No issue working in another regional state later; the 191 pathway is not tied to staying in the nominating state.

note: Still awaiting a 491 NSW grant; planning to relocate to a regional NSW city and look for IT or trade work.

title: Offshore 491 invite chances for SA business development role
note: Asking about realistic points and timing for an offshore 491 SA invitation in an ICT management occupation on the state list.

comments.body: Suggested applying broadly across 491, 189 and 190 since 491 allocations are being cut; some recent invites seen around 100 to 110 points.

note: Primary applicant lodged a company-sponsored 482, submitted requested extra documents in February, but is still under further assessment.

comments.body: Another applicant noted being in the same situation, lodged in February with status still showing as received.

note: Reported the 482 was granted after about 119 days of waiting, encouraging others to stay hopeful.
Lodged a medium-term 482 in late February, received an S56 a week later for police and medical, submitted both, and is still waiting.
Transferred from a short-term 482; lodged a medium-term 482 in March, got an S56 for medical, completed it in April, still under further assessment past the processing window.

title: Subclass 500 subsequent-entrant dependent processing time
note: Master's student lodged a subclass 500 subsequent-entrant application for a spouse in late April; asking whether proposed July changes affect dependent processing.

comments.body: Others reported lodging in March and May for partners and still waiting with no outcome.

note: Spouse of a higher-education student; lodged own application in early May, completed health check and biometrics mid-May, still no decision by August.
Subsequent-entrant subclass 500 in the higher-education sector was granted in early October after lodging in mid-June.

title: 189 invitation received, next steps and document checklist
note: Received a 189 invitation onshore with 90 points; asking about the lodgement process, whether to do medicals upfront, and what documents to upload.

comments.body: Advised generating a HAP ID, completing medicals, and uploading Form 80, 1221 and supporting documents upfront to aim for a direct grant.

replies.body: Noted that waiting for case-officer contact can push the grant back by weeks or months.

note: Onshore engineer; full DE journey from skills assessment to grant in about four months, with an info request after nomination approval.

comments.body: Another member asked what the case officer requested in the s56.

replies.body: Applicant replied the officer wanted licensing/registration evidence and work history proof such as payslips and tax documents.

note: Primary applicant onshore with offshore dependents; nomination and visa lodged together, granted in about two months.
Offshore applicant with two dependents; nomination and visa lodged together, both approved in roughly two months.
Onshore applicant lodged nomination and visa together with health check done a week later; no department updates yet.
Nomination lodged in late July and visa lodged in late August with police and medicals included; awaiting any update.

title: Secondary applicant relocating and 191 eligibility timing on a joint 491
note: Couple granted a NSW-nominated 491; asks whether the secondary applicant can move regionally first, live outside the nominating state, and how staggered residence affects 191 eligibility.

comments.body: A responder said re-entry is fine once entry conditions are met and that living/working in any designated regional area satisfies the conditions; the nominating-state commitment is moral rather than legal.

replies.body: Original poster thanked them and said it was helpful.

note: Offshore family of five; visa granted after about 28 months with four separate document requests, the last answered in mid-2025.

comments.body: Another waiting applicant congratulated them and asked whether the document requests came in different months and what each was for.

Lodged mid-2023; received a document request in Aug 2025 for partner's English plus a re-medical, all cleared and submitted within days; no further update.

comments.body: Consider engaging a registered migration agent who specialises in education visas.
A large gap since prior study and tightened student-visa risk settings can make approval harder.

note: Skilled nominated applicant lodged in April 2019, received a case officer request for an employment reference, responded next day, still awaiting grant nine months on.

replies.body: Asked to be kept posted on any movement.

replies.body: Confirmed they were lodged together in this case.

title: Subclass 186 stuck in external security checks for over a year
note: Employer-sponsored applicant lodged in February 2015, had a case officer information request in June 2015, and after a year is still waiting on external security checks with no timeline.

comments.body: A reply noted external security checks are typically lengthy, often adding around a year, with no way to speed them up.

title: When does the partner-visa bridging visa activate after an onshore 820 lodgement?
note: Sponsor asks when a bridging visa activates after lodging an onshore partner application for a spouse who entered on a visitor visa; later confirms the bridging visa became active and work rights applied.

comments.body: A reply cautioned that marrying onshore after entering on a tourist visa may draw extra scrutiny and risk refusal.

replies.body: Original poster said an agent advised the bridging visa should activate after about three months.

note: 189 applicant with 75 points; case officer assigned about six weeks after lodging, still awaiting a decision.
189 applicant invited at 70 points; case officer requested relationship, character and partner English evidence, granted after response.

comments.body: Another member asked whether the partner had to retake the English test in response to the case officer request.

title: Can lodging a second work visa affect a pending 189 application?
note: Applicant with a lodged 189 asks whether also applying for a separate temporary work visa would delay or jeopardise the pending PR case.

comments.body: One reply suggested the two applications are independent and can be processed separately.
Another warned that holding a later work visa could invalidate the earlier PR application.

title: How to handle health insurance when lodging a 485 from offshore
note: Recent graduate applying for a 485 from outside Australia with student visa just expired asks how to meet health cover requirements while borders are closed.

comments.body: A reply explained offshore applicants can buy a policy with a future start date and submit a cover letter showing genuine intent, extending the date if processing runs long.
Another noted the post-study work stream had a 6 to 12 month processing time and required having held a student visa within the past 12 months.

title: Can the 485 stream be changed after lodging?
note: Graduate who lodged a 485 under the graduate work stream but wanted the post-study work stream asks whether the stream can be switched.

comments.body: Replies said the stream cannot be changed after applying.
One suggested withdrawing the current application, applying again under the correct stream, and managing the resulting bridging visa transition.

title: Including an offshore spouse as a dependent on a 485 application
note: Applicant asks about adding an offshore spouse as a dependent to a partner's upcoming 485 application lodged from onshore.

comments.body: A reply confirmed the spouse can be added as a dependent with proof of relationship and would receive the same visa, but offshore travel depends on border status.

note: Onshore Direct Entry applicant waiting on nomination approval roughly six months after lodging; second applicant added and health completed.

comments.body: Asked whether the applicant is onshore or offshore and whether the sponsoring employer holds accredited status.

Onshore Melbourne Direct Entry applicant with an accredited sponsor and three dependents; health done, status received with no further movement.
Onshore Melbourne Direct Entry applicant with an accredited sponsor and dependents; health completed early, application silent on status received.

title: How does a sponsoring employer being acquired affect a 482 visa and the path to 186 PR?
note: Sponsored worker asks whether an employer takeover requires a fresh nomination and whether the two-year work requirement for PR transition must be with the same employer.

comments.body: A new nomination from the acquiring company is likely needed; consult a registered migration agent.

replies.body: With over three years of experience the Direct Entry stream is an option if skills assessment and English results are positive.

note: Offshore student visa applicant for a commercial cookery course; contacted with questions a week after lodging, still waiting about seven weeks later.

comments.body: Asked what questions the department raised during the call.

replies.body: The applicant said they were asked about course choice given their age and about source of funds.

Lodged late June with medicals and police checks completed; no case officer contact yet.

note: Onshore; state pre-invite mid May, lodged early June, medicals cleared days later, grant late August with no case officer contact.
Onshore; state pre-invite early May, lodged early June, medicals cleared next day, direct grant mid September after about three months.
Onshore; state pre-invite early March, nomination and lodgement May, medicals cleared mid June; awaiting case officer.

comments.body: Asks whether a passport-size photo is mandatory after an agent left it off the application.

replies.body: Others confirm the photo is required and suggest checking the application in the immigration account directly.

title: Sponsored visitor visa refused while offshore partner application pending
note: A sponsored family visitor visa was refused on genuine-temporary-stay grounds while a partner application was pending; asks what other options exist.

comments.body: Notes the refusal turned on doubts the applicant would return home, and suggests a tribunal review or a more precise reapplication with strong evidence of intent to depart.

replies.body: Explains that applying for a partner visa signals intent to settle, which undermines a visitor application and is a common reason for such refusals.

title: Student visa extension refused; considering a partner visa application
note: An applicant whose student visa extension was refused after marrying asks whether switching to a partner visa is viable or could be harmful.

comments.body: Responder asks about the immigration status of the partner before advising.

title: Received natural justice notice that sponsor has no approved nomination on 482 application
note: On a bridging visa, applicant received a natural-justice notice stating the sponsor lacks an approved nomination; asks about causes, timing to fix, and fallback visa options.

comments.body: Suggests employer-sponsored applications are usually handled by a registered agent and recommends contacting them.

replies.body: Explains employers must be approved sponsors first; lack of detail from the employer is a warning sign, and advises consulting a registered agent on pathways.

title: Can a 485 applicant leave Australia and wait offshore for the grant
note: Onshore applicant asks whether they can lodge a 485 then return home to wait, or if they must remain onshore for the decision.

comments.body: Responder notes applicants must be in Australia when the decision is made and cautions that leaving may prevent return, so staying onshore is advised.
